title: Universal injectivity into a flat target tested on ideal quotients
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $L,M$ be $R$-modules, let $M$ be flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and let $v:L\to M$ be $R$-linear. For an ideal $J\subseteq R$, write $JL$ for the submodule generated by all $a\ell$ with $a\in J$, $\ell\in L$, and similarly define $JM$. Then the following are equivalent: (i) for every $R$-module $Q$, the map $v\otimes1_Q:L\otimes_RQ\to M\otimes_RQ$ is injective [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; (ii) for every finitely generated ideal $J$ of $R$, the induced map $L/JL\to M/JM$ is injective. No finite generation or flatness assumption on $L$ is imposed.

proof.text: We use tensor factors in the order $Q\otimes_R X$. The bilinear rule $x\otimes q\mapsto q\otimes x$ gives an isomorphism with inverse the same rule, and commutes with $v$ on pure tensors, by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For any ideal $I$ and module $X$, define $\alpha_{I,X}:(R/I)\otimes_R X\to X/IX$ by $\bar a\otimes x\mapsto ax\bmod IX$. This is well-defined and bilinear since changing $a$ by an element of $I$ changes $ax$ by an element of $IX$. Its inverse is $x\bmod IX\mapsto\bar1\otimes x$: it kills $IX$ since $\bar1\otimes ax=\bar a\otimes x=0$ for $a\in I$. The composites fix $x\bmod IX$ and $\bar a\otimes x$ respectively, hence are identities because pure tensors generate. These isomorphisms identify $1_{R/I}\otimes v$ with the induced map $L/IL\to M/IM$, since both send $\bar a\otimes\ell$ to $av(\ell)\bmod IM$.

source.place: Tag 0AS5, cyclic tensor identifications, expanded from the tensor universal property, Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product).

proof.text: If (i) holds, apply it with $Q=R/J$ and use Step 1 to obtain (ii). Conversely assume (ii). We first extend its conclusion to an arbitrary ideal $I$. If $v(\ell)\in IM$, write $v(\ell)=\sum_{j=1}^t a_jm_j$ with $a_j\in I$. The ideal $J=(a_1,\ldots,a_t)$ is finitely generated and contained in $I$. Thus $v(\ell)\in JM$, so (ii) gives $\ell\in JL\subseteq IL$. Therefore $L/IL\to M/IM$ is injective for every ideal $I$, and Step 1 gives injectivity of $1_{R/I}\otimes v$ for every $I$. The empty sum uses $J=0$, which is finitely generated.

source.place: Tag 0AS5, final paragraph: passage from finitely generated ideals to all ideals; direct finite-sum version of the filtered-colimit argument.

proof.text: Fix a finitely presented $R$-module $Q$. By [def-sc-finitely-presented-module] it admits a surjection $R^n\to Q$; let $q_1,\ldots,q_n$ be the images of the basis vectors. Put $Q_i=Rq_1+\cdots+Rq_i$, so $Q_0=0$ and $Q_n=Q$. For each $1\le i\le n$, put $I_i=\{a\in R:aq_i\in Q_{i-1}\}$. This is an ideal by closure of $Q_{i-1}$ under addition and scalar multiplication. The map $R/I_i\to Q_i/Q_{i-1}$, $\bar a\mapsto aq_i\bmod Q_{i-1}$, is well-defined, surjective by $Q_i=Q_{i-1}+Rq_i$, and injective by the definition of $I_i$. Consequently $C_i=Q_i/Q_{i-1}$ is a cyclic module isomorphic to $R/I_i$; its tensor map $1_{C_i}\otimes v$ is injective by Step 2. No assertion that $I_i$ is finitely generated is needed.

source.place: Tag 00KZ (lemma-trivial-filter-finite-module), explicit filtration by a finite generating list, as used in Tag 0AS5.

proof.text: For $X=L$ and for $X=M$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] to $Q_{i-1}\xrightarrow{a_i}Q_i\xrightarrow{b_i}C_i\to0$. This gives exact rows $Q_{i-1}\otimes_R X\xrightarrow{a_i\otimes1_X}Q_i\otimes_R X\xrightarrow{b_i\otimes1_X}C_i\otimes_R X\to0$. Since $a_i$ is injective and $M$ is flat, [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] also makes $a_i\otimes1_M$ injective. Set $v_T=1_T\otimes v$. The squares commute: on a pure tensor $q\otimes\ell$, either route in the $a_i$ square is $a_i(q)\otimes v(\ell)$, and either route in the $b_i$ square is $b_i(q)\otimes v(\ell)$; equality on all tensors follows from [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Tag 0AS5, displayed tensor diagram; Tag 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact) and Tag 00HB (definition-flat).

proof.text: Induct on $i$ to prove $v_{Q_i}$ injective. For $i=0$ its source is zero: each pure tensor with first factor in $0$ is zero. Suppose $v_{Q_{i-1}}$ is injective and let $z\in Q_i\otimes_R L$ satisfy $v_{Q_i}(z)=0$. Its image $c=(b_i\otimes1_L)(z)$ satisfies $v_{C_i}(c)=0$ by the right square of Step 4, so $c=0$ by Step 3. Exactness of the upper row gives $y\in Q_{i-1}\otimes_R L$ with $(a_i\otimes1_L)(y)=z$. The left square now gives $(a_i\otimes1_M)(v_{Q_{i-1}}(y))=0$. Injectivity of $a_i\otimes1_M$ gives $v_{Q_{i-1}}(y)=0$, and the induction hypothesis gives $y=0$, hence $z=0$. Thus $v_{Q_n}=v_Q$ is injective. The base-case tensor identity follows from bilinearity in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Tag 0AS5, sentence "A simple induction argument": full element chase in the two exact rows.

proof.text: We have proved $1_Q\otimes v$ injective for every finitely presented $R$-module $Q$, without any Noetherian assumption on $R$. Apply the first equivalence of [lem-trf-universal-injective-finite-test] to conclude injectivity for every $R$-module $Q$. The factor-swapping isomorphisms of Step 1 give exactly $v\otimes1_Q$ injective, which is (i).
